models_evaluated: Fusion multimodal with NLP Random Forest delirium risk stratification model

links.outcome: Discrimination at external site vs development site without retraining
links.effect: AUROC 0.91 (95% CI 0.90-0.92) at MSM vs 0.94 (0.93-0.94) at MSH, with no retraining.
links.quote: In this quality improvement study, an ML-enabled delirium risk stratification model demonstrated good discriminative performance statistics at MSM, comparable to contemporaneous performance at the model development site (MSH) during the same 12-month period of live clinical practice and to previous internal validation at MSH after model training and testing.

links.outcome: False positives and alert burden at operational thresholds
links.effect: PPV 25.9% at MSM (threshold 0.50) and 19.4% at MSH (threshold 0.55). There were 1381 false positives at MSM, and the authors note a risk of alert fatigue.
links.quote: Even with the transferred model, the PPV is 26%, which could lead to a high volume of false positives.

links.outcome: Delirium detection rate when risk scores prioritize CAM assessments
links.effect: Adjusted OR 1.63 (95% CI 1.37-1.94). Mean monthly detection rate rose from 9.23% to 19.59% after deployment (P < .001).
links.quote: Adjusted logistic regression indicated a significant increase in the odds of delirium being detected after deployment of the ML-based delirium model compared with the predeployment period (adjusted odds ratio, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.37-1.94; P < .001).

models_evaluated: Fusion multimodal with natural language processing delirium risk stratification model (Random Forest)

links.outcome: Discriminative performance across external and development hospitals
links.effect: AUROC was 0.91 (95% CI, 0.90-0.92) at MSM versus 0.94 (95% CI, 0.93-0.94) at MSH; discrimination remained strong without retraining despite the modest cross-site difference.
links.quote: The AUROC of the model was 0.91 (95% CI, 0.90-0.92) for MSM and 0.94 (95% CI, 0.93-0.94) for MSH.

links.outcome: False-positive risk classifications at operational thresholds
links.effect: At operational thresholds 0.50 (MSM) and 0.55 (MSH), PPV was 25.9% and 19.4%; false positives numbered 1381 and 2234, respectively. Alert fatigue itself was not measured.
links.quote: The model had a PPV of 25.9% (482 / [482 + 1381]) for MSM and 19.4% (538 / [538 + 2234]) for MSH.

links.outcome: Delirium diagnostic yield after AI-guided prioritization of standardized assessments
links.effect: Monthly detection increased from 9.23% to 19.59% (P < .001); adjusted odds ratio, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.37-1.94. This was an uncontrolled pre-post comparison.
links.quote: Adjusted logistic regression indicated a significant increase in the odds of delirium being detected after deployment of the ML-based delirium model compared with the predeployment period (adjusted odds ratio, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.37-1.94; P < .001).

screen.practice: external validation at a new site without retraining
screen.reason: The study evaluates the live clinical deployment and external validation of an ML delirium risk model across hospitals, tracking clinical detection rates and discrimination, but it does not compare outcomes with and without a specific deployment safeguard or practice.
